question: When an acid is allowed to react with a base to form salt and water, this chemical reaction is named as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**neutralisation reaction**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Neutralisation reaction** is the chemical reaction where an **acid reacts with a base to form salt and water**.
 
• In this reaction, the H⁺ ion from the acid combines with the OH⁻ ion from the base to produce water (H₂O).
